newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves a host of China investments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves a host of China investments.

text.p: Taiwan on Tuesday approved a wide range of investments in arch-rival China, but maintained a ban on major infrastructure projects.

The economics ministry said in a statement it had authorised investments in 411 new industry categories. Among them are travel agencies, hotels, recreation facilities, warehouses and cement plants. The total amount of the planned investments was not given.
Infrastructure projects now placed on the ministry's "ban list" included railroads, highways, ports, airports, water works, power plants and incinerators.
The ministry said the restrictions aimed to prevent Taiwan from becoming too dependent on China, the island's political rival since a civil war the two sides in 1949.
"These investments (if approved) may have negative effects on domestic economic development and our national defence security," the ministry said.
Beijing sees Taiwan as a renegade province to be brought under the mainland's eventual rule, by force if necessary.

Taiwan, which has banned direct links with China since 1949, has since the late 1980s allowed US$30 billion worth of "indirect" investments to be routed into the mainland through a third territory, usually Hong Kong.
The ministry's Investment Commission had said that the 411 newly sanctioned categories would increase the number of mainland investment categories that require explicit commission approval to 2,477.
A total of 4,350 investments types are now permitted for mainland investment, while 299 items remain forbidden.
The ban on power plants put an end to Formosa Plastics Group's plan to invest $3 billion in building a 3,600-megawatt thermal power complex in Zhangzhou in China's southern province of Fujian.
Formosa had said it would "patiently wait" for a shift in policy by Taiwan's Nationalist government.
